Maintenance Report — MNT-0131-011

Asset: WELL-0131 (NE-07 Well 131, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 11 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 29 Oct 2024 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 443 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0131-0103 on 2024-10-10 Report written: 30 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0131-0103 showed the wellhead at 27.4 °C with the air at 22.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly2,391
Bolts, shims and seals598
Bearing grease and consumables996
Labour (company crew)2,395
Total6,380

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0131-018

Asset: WELL-0131 (NE-07 Well 131, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Feb 2026 08:00 · Finished: 18 Feb 2026 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 80 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0131-0170 on 2026-02-12 Report written: 19 Feb 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0131-0170 showed the wellhead at 11.9 °C with the air at 10.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 340 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 272 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0131-018 (WS-06).

  • Check wall thickness along the rest of this flowline.
  • Consider corrosion inhibitor injection.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0131-020

Asset: WELL-0131 (NE-07 Well 131, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 17 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 17 Apr 2026 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 12 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0131-0179 on 2026-04-16 Report written: 19 Apr 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0131-0179 at 14:15 on 2026-04-16 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.7% of the pad area, estimated 2.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 340 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 272 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0131-020 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.56% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
